header:
Date: 2026-03-05 | Time: 15:00 PT | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Aya Patel (Redwood Solutions), Daniel Kim (Orbit - Head ML), Rita Morales (Orbit - PM), Samir Iqbal (Orbit - Eng Lead)
summary: POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan: define golden prompts, regression test suite, hallucination detection/format checks, scoring approach and timelines. Agreed to run a 1,000 prompt benchmark then expand to 10k if initial pass succeeds. Key constraints: latency targets for user-facing flows (<=350ms p95), data residency concerns for EU users, and limited labeling bandwidth on customer side.
topics: Introductions; current stack and traffic profile; success criteria; dataset and sample extraction; golden prompt construction; regression and hallucination checks; scoring & pass/fail thresholds; timeline and next steps.
transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call... 
[00:08] Daniel Kim: Hi all, Daniel here. 
[00:12] Rita Morales: Rita. 
[00:15] Samir Iqbal: Samir. 
[00:18] Marco Ruiz: Marco from Redwood SE. 
[00:20] Aya Patel: Aya on Solutions. 
[00:25] Laura Chen: Cool. Objective for today is to align on the quality eval playbook for the proof-of-concept, especially the golden prompts and how we'll measure regressions and hallucinations. 
[00:40] Daniel Kim: High level, our product has two primary flows: a customer support summarization and an internal triage assistant. Latency matters more for triage because it's used in live ops. 
[00:55] Rita Morales: And we need outputs to follow strict formatting - JSON payloads with enumerated fields; if the model deviates we have downstream parsing failures. 
[01:10] Marco Ruiz: Noted. When you say strict JSON, is there a schema you can share? 
[01:18] Samir Iqbal: We'll upload the schema, but to be clear we do allow small deviations as long as there's an easy fallback — though we'd prefer avoid branching logic. 
[01:30] Laura Chen: Ok so success criteria draft: 1) functional correctness (format adherence) >= 99% on golden prompts; 2) hallucination rate <= 0.5% on defined factual checks; 3) latency p95 <= 350ms on hosted path; 4) semantic quality score (human eval) average >= 4/5 on support cases. Thoughts? 
[01:58] Daniel Kim: The 0.5% hallucination threshold seems tight but reasonable for core facts. For support summarization we actually tolerate slightly more hallucination if it doesn't invent actionable items. 
[02:12] Rita Morales: Format adherence is non-negotiable. Our parser will drop records that don't match. 
[02:20] Marco Ruiz: For format checks we'll do automated regex + JSON schema validation as the first gate, then a second gate of lightweight semantic checks (e.g. entity overlap). 
[02:33] Aya Patel: On golden prompts: we'll create 30-50 canonical prompts per flow that represent edge cases, typical happy path, and adversarial malformed inputs. Redwood will propose an initial set. 
[02:48] Samir Iqbal: Can you also include noisy transcripts, partial sentences, and non-English fragments? We get messy input. 
[02:57] Marco Ruiz: Yes, include noise variants. Also we'll include prompt permutations: system instruction tweaks, temperature changes, and max tokens. 
[03:10] Laura Chen: Benchmark plan: run 1k prompts through candidate models (open quantized variants + a baseline) — measure format pass rate, hallucination checks, BLEU-ish overlap, and a human semantic rubric on 200 sampled responses. If pass threshold met, expand to 10k with stratified sampling. 
[03:33] Daniel Kim: Who will label hallucinations? We have limited labelers. 
[03:38] Laura Chen: Good point — propose a hybrid: automated heuristics for easy cases, and Redwood will provide a labeling UI for manual adjudication. Customer provides 200 gold-labeled examples up front for calibration. 
[03:50] Rita Morales: We can produce 200 gold-labeled tickets in 2 weeks, but more will be costly. 
[03:56] Marco Ruiz: That's enough to calibrate scoring. Scoring approach: weighted metric vector — format adherence (40%), factual consistency/hallucination (30%), semantic quality (20%), latency (10%). We'll report per-flow breakdowns and an overall pass score. 
[04:15] Samir Iqbal: How do we define pass? Thresholds per metric? 
[04:19] Marco Ruiz: Yes. Example: overall pass >= 85/100, with floor constraints: format >= 99%, hallucination <= 0.5%, latency p95 <= 350ms. Those floors must be met regardless of overall score. 
[04:33] Aya Patel: Regression testing: we will snapshot golden prompt outputs and run nightly diff on new model builds — plus smoke tests on core intents. We'll also track token-level drift and perplexity baselines. 
[04:48] Daniel Kim: For hallucination detection, can you run a named-entity cross-check against our product catalog? 
[04:54] Marco Ruiz: Yes, if you share a product catalog we can run entity verification as part of the automated hallucination heuristics. 
[05:02] Rita Morales: There's also GDPR/residency constraints for EU customers; some data cannot leave the EU region. 
[05:08] Laura Chen: Noted — for the POC we'll keep EU traffic in the EU region or run through Redwood Private if needed. We'll include a short checklist for residency options. 
[05:18] Samir Iqbal: What models are you proposing for the baseline? 
[05:22] Marco Ruiz: We'll test two quantized open models (one 8-bit, one 4-bit candidate) plus Redwood-catalog baseline (vino-1 small) — the point is to show cost/latency/quality tradeoffs. 
[05:36] Daniel Kim: Cost is important. Can you show token-level cost and expected monthly spend for our projected 1M messages/month? 
[05:42] Laura Chen: Yes we'll include a cost model in the follow-up doc. Expect tokenization differences depending on prompts. 
[05:50] Rita Morales: Timeline? 
[05:52] Laura Chen: Proposed timeline: week 1 (Mar 8-14): data share and golden prompt draft; week 2 (Mar 15-21): initial 1k benchmark and human eval on 200 samples; week 3 (Mar 22-28): tune/policy and run expanded 10k; week 4 (Mar 29-Apr 4): final report and handoff. Adjust if needed. 
[06:18] Samir Iqbal: That seems aggressive but doable. We'll push the sample export this week. 
[06:25] Marco Ruiz: On tooling: Redwood will provide a lightweight runner and a results dashboard. We'll also include a CSV export of per-prompt judgments. 
[06:35] Daniel Kim: For regression tests, how do you handle false positives from minor phrasing changes? 
[06:40] Marco Ruiz: We use thresholded similarity — small paraphrases won't fail if semantic similarity > 0.85 and format is correct. 
[06:48] Rita Morales: Also need to surface examples where hallucination is subtle — like inventing an action item. 
[06:52] Aya Patel: We'll include a hallucination taxonomy in the playbook: factual invention, entity swap, hallucinated dates, invented steps, and missing required fields. Each has different severity weights. 
[07:06] Laura Chen: Great. Anything else? 
[07:09] Samir Iqbal: One ask: can Redwood run a mock streaming scenario to measure tail latency with concurrent sessions? 
[07:15] Marco Ruiz: Yes — we can simulate 100 concurrent short sessions to get p95/p99. It will increase infra time but doable for the POC. 
[07:24] Laura Chen: Ok recap of next steps: Laura sends golden prompt draft + rubric + security checklist; Samir sends sample traffic and schema; Marco sets up benchmark runner and schedules the 1k run for week of Mar 16. 
[07:38] Daniel Kim: Thanks all, appreciate it. 
[07:40] Laura Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with timeline and calendar invites. 
[07:44] [end]
notes: Shared artifacts: Redwood playbook draft (link: https://redwood.ai/playbooks/orbit-golden-prompts-draft), sample benchmark spreadsheet to be created, security checklist link. Customer emphasized format correctness and residency. Agreed initial 1k benchmark then 10k expansion. Hybrid labeling approach for hallucination adjudication.
closing_summary: Aligned on POC quality eval structure: golden prompts (30-50 per flow), automated format/schema checks + semantic heuristics, weighted scoring with hard floors, initial 1k benchmark and 200 human eval samples, timeline roughly 3-4 weeks. Action owners assigned and next steps scheduled.
